'''Traian V. Chirilă''' (born 14 February 1948 in [[Arad, Romania|Arad]], [[Socialist Republic of Romania|Romania]])<ref name=ziarulcrisul /> is a Romanian-Australian [[Polymer chemistry|polymer]] and [[Organic chemistry|organic chemist]] who is the inventor of [[Corneal transplantation#AlphaCor|AlphaCor]], an [[Keratoprosthesis|artificial cornea]] in current clinical use throughout the world.<ref name=qei />

His past and current research has contributed in several areas of [[biomaterial]]s, [[polymer science]] and [[Biological engineering|bioengineering]], especially in the understanding of biomaterials and [[biocompatibility]], in the development of [[polymer]]s, hydrophilic sponges, [[artificial cornea]], artificial vitreous substitutes and in topics such as interaction of laser radiation with polymers, photoresponsive polymers, [[supramolecular polymers]], sustained release of bioactive agents, tissue engineering and the use of polymers in genetic therapies.<ref name=qei>{{cite web|url=http://www.qei.org.au/research/our-researchers/|title=Research – Our Researchers – Professor Traian Chirila|work=Queensland Eye Institute|access-date=4 October 2014|archive-date=6 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006162256/http://www.qei.org.au/research/our-researchers/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Chirilă was born and educated in Romania, where he obtained a [[BEng]] in [[polymer technology]] (1972) and a PhD in [[organic chemistry]] (1981) from the [[Polytechnic University of Timișoara]].{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}

After ten years of research in polymers and organic chemistry, he relocated to Australia. During 1984 he was a [[research fellow]] at the Curtin School of Applied Chemistry. In 1986 he joined [[Lions Eye Institute]] in [[Perth]] as a senior scientist with the task of establishing a department for research and development of polymeric [[biomaterial]]s for [[ophthalmology]]. In 2005, he joined the newly founded Queensland Eye Institute in [[Brisbane]], where he was offered a position of senior scientist to continue his research and to establish a department of ophthalmic [[Biological engineering|bioengineering]]. He was made a fellow of [[Royal Australian Chemical Institute]] (RACI) in 1992. Currently, he holds three adjunct professorships at the School of Physical and Chemical Sciences of [[Queensland University of Technology]], Australian Institute for Bioengineering and Nanotechnology of [[University of Queensland]], and Faculty of Health Sciences of University of Queensland.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}

==Research==
* Contributions to the synthetic and structural chemistry of acetals, especially cyclic acetals.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Studies of hydrogels containing UV-absorbing agents. Correlating the concentration, absorptive properties and extractability of the agents.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Interaction of polymers with IR laser radiation – demonstrating that the monomer release following the irradiation of IOL materials with surgical IR lasers is too low to cause deleterious effects in the eye.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* First investigation of interaction between poly(2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate) (PHEMA) and UV laser radiation. First use of X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to investigate the process of ablation of ophthalmic hydrogels with excimer lasers. General studies on the interaction between high-energy laser radiation and polymers.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Invention and development of melanin-containing synthetic hydrogels able to absorb UV and blue radiation and their application as IOL materials. First polymer-biopolymer combinations to be reported as interpenetrating polymer networks (IPNs).{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Invention and development of an artificial cornea. Initially known as "Chirila keratoprosthesis", this device has been commercially developed as [[Corneal transplantation#AlphaCor|AlphaCor]] and received approvals from FDA and other regulatory bodies and is used in human patients.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Development of hydrogels with very high water content as potential substitutes for the vitreous body, including a methodology for their evaluation in vitro.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Evaluation of porous hydrogel scaffolds for nerve repair.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Development and study of polymer matrices for the sustained release of bioactive agents, including therapeutic oligonucleotides.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Development of an orbital implant, currently commercialised as [[AlphaSphere (medical implant)|AlphaSphere]].{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Contributions to the history of ophthalmology and biomaterials.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}
* Development of tissue-engineered corneal constructs for the restoration of ocular surface.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}

His research has resulted to date in 175 journal publications and 13 patents. He has contributed over 175 presentations at scientific meetings and he has been invited to present lectures in China, the United States, Japan, Romania, Italy, France, Switzerland, Korea, Germany and The Netherlands.{{citation needed|date=October 2014}}

==Personal life==
He spent his childhood in a small town in Transylvania, [[Chișineu-Criș]], graduating from the local high school in 1966. He is nicknamed "Tanu". His mother died in 2019 while still living in Timisoara, Romania where he graduated from the university. Traian is married to Mika, who is from Japan, and they have a son, Sebastian.<ref name=ziarulcrisul>{{cite web|url=http://www.ziarulcrisul.ro/articol/traian-chirila-om-de-stiinta-de-prestigiu-si-inventatorul-unei-cornee-artificiale/3050|title=Traian Chirilă, om de ştiinţă de prestigiu şi inventatorul unei cornee artificiale|publisher=Ziarul Crișul|date=24 January 2014|language=Romanian|access-date=4 October 2014|archive-date=6 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006115401/http://www.ziarulcrisul.ro/articol/traian-chirila-om-de-stiinta-de-prestigiu-si-inventatorul-unei-cornee-artificiale/3050|url-status=dead}}</ref>
